content.summary_of_the_paper:
The paper proposes a method to improve traffic speed prediction innovatively with causal discovery and conduct experiments on two real-world public datasets, achieving promising performance.

Contributions

(1) It is cutting-edge work to apply causal observation for spatiotemporal forecasting. The authors define legitimate traffic variables for causal structure discovery and conduct experiments on the PEMS-BAY dataset to learn their causal relations. 

(2) The framework effectively captures spatial-temporal dependencies and validate its performance on two real-world public datasets. 
Strength and weaknesses
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros:

(1) It is a good idea to consider causal observation for spatiotemporal forecasting.

(2) The authors conduct comprehensive experiments both on the modules designed and parameter analysis such as (the number of stacking GT layers.

Cons:

(1) The motivation of the causal insight layer is not clear and convincing enough. The difference between causal correlations and spatio-temporal correlations is not clarified explicitly.

(2) The result using historical one-hour speed data for 15min ahead speed forecasting is not satisfactory enough. It is doubtful whether the degradation in performance is due to the removal of the causal insight layer or the reduction in model complexity. It should be explained whether the causality relation discovered with dataset PEMS-BAY can be generalized as well on all datasets.

(3) Some notations are unintelligible to understand. And the notation in Figure 2 is also puzzling, whether the "t_i" means the speed or the time.

(4) It would be better if the dimensionality of Q could be extended to more features.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The overall structure and presentation of the paper are clear and it is innovative in integrating the idea of causal discovery into traffic forecasting with high reproducibility.
content.summary_of_the_review: The authors propose a good idea to apply causal discovery to traffic prediction. However, the motivation of the causal insight layer and the difference between it and spatio-temporal relations are not illustrated clearly. Moreover, the improvement in performance is slight compared to the baselines. Overall, this paper is not good enough.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposed a framework to integrate causality with spatial-temporal information for traffic prediction.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. The writing is clear and easy to follow.
2. The figure illustration is informative.

Weaknesses
1. The novelty is limited. Although the paper claimed to integrate causality, only utilizing statistical tools discover causal structures among nodes. The causality discovery and the model part are separated. For combining causality, spatial correlations and temporal dependencies, there is no surprise to see concatenation and attention.
2. R2 is not evaluated. Only checking the errors is not reliable.
3. Table 1, in some cases, the proposed model cannot beat baseline algorithms, which is against the claim in the paper "that GT-CausIn significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art models".
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The writing is clear. But the novelty is limited. Appendix F only shows partial hyperparameter settings, which makes the reproducibility doubtful.
content.summary_of_the_review: While the writing is clear, the technical contribution is limited, the experiment setting cannot fully support the claims of the paper.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a "casual insight"-based model named GT-CausIn for traffic speed prediction. Its core idea is to add a self-attention layer to learn the spatial relationships between the traffic patterns of neighbouring nodes on a traffic sensor network. The first and the second order neighbours are considered in the model, and the variation in the traffic speed in two consecutive time slices (the causal insight) are used as the input features of every node. Experimental results on two real data sets show that the proposed model is effective especially for predictions for 30 and 60 minutes ahead of time.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. The paper proposes a model that is shown to be effective on real datasets. 

2. A causal discovery experiment is run that finds that speed variation is an important feature for traffic pattern modelling.

Weakness:
1. The paper puts together the DCRNN model (Li et al., 2018) with a self-attention module (which was used in GMAN (Zheng et al., 2020) but with a different input). The technical novelty is unclear beyond finding that speed variation is a useful feature for traffic prediction. 

2. Following on Point 1, while there is an ablation study to show the importance of the speed variation features, there is no study to show the importance of using the self-attention layer together with such input features.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper is readable in general. It can use a proofread to improve its readability. For example, the paper can clarify early on that casual discovery is not part of the proposed traffic prediction model. Instead, it was used to find a new input feature (traffic speed variation) for traffic prediction models. 

It would be interesting to see if the traffic speed variation features can be used in existing traffic prediction models to improve their prediction performance. 

Grammar:
"end up with a detailed introduction of its crucial component layers" => "end with a detailed introduction of its crucial component layers"
"differentiating adjacent time slices" => "taking the difference in speed between adjacent time slices"
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper uses casual discovery to identify that traffic speed variation is an effective feature for traffic speed prediction, and it uses such features with a self-attention layer on top of the DCRNN model. The technical novelty and depth are both quite limited.

content.title: GT-CausIn: a novel causal-based insight for traffic prediction
content.abstract: Traffic forecasting is an important issue of spatiotemporal series prediction. Among different methods, graph neural networks have achieved so far the most promising results, learning relations between graph nodes then becomes a crucial task. However, improvement space is very limited when these relations are learned in a node-to-node manner. The challenge stems from (1) obscure temporal dependencies between different stations, (2) difficulties in defining variables beyond the node level, and (3) no ready-made method to validate the learned relations. To confront these challenges, we define legitimate traffic variables to discover the causal structure of the traffic network. The causal relation is carefully checked with statistic tools and case analysis. We then present a novel model named Graph Spatial-Temporal Network Based on Causal Insight (GT-CausIn), where graph diffusion layers and temporal convolutional network (TCN) layers are integrated with causal knowledge to capture dependencies in spatiotemporal space. Experiments are carried out on two real-world traffic datasets: PEMS-BAY and METR-LA, which show that GT-CausIn significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art models.
